frames.narration: Both devices hold the same record: title, notes, due, status, priority. Each change is sent as a mutation with an id, not as a whole new record.
At minute 15 device B loses its connection. Its edits are applied to its local record and appended to the outbox, in order, each with an id (B-1, B-2...).
Meanwhile device A is online. It edits the notes and the status, and the server applies both at once.
B keeps going: two more edits, status and title. Now B holds 4 mutations. B and A both changed the notes and the status without knowing about each other.
Minute 35: B reconnects and replays the outbox in order. The server applies each id once. If an acknowledgement is lost and B resends, the repeated id is ignored.
Due and title changed on one side only, so they merge. Notes and status changed on both sides: that is a conflict, and the policy decides what happens.

With last writer wins by timestamp, the whole record of the newest clock replaces the other: 2 of A's edits vanish, silently. A wrong clock on B flips the winner, and then B's edits to due and title, which A never touched, vanish too.
With per-field merge, only the clashing fields need a rule, and notes can be joined. With 'ask the user', the server keeps both versions and the user chooses, so nothing is lost.
